units.rightText: And it shall be as when a hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.

units.leftText: Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
units.rightText: Tarry ye and wonder; take your pleasure and be blind: they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.

units.leftText: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes, the prophets; and he has covered your heads, the seers.
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes, the prophets; and your heads, the seers, hath he covered.

units.leftText: All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is educated, saying, “Read this, please;” and he says, “I can’t, for it is sealed;”
units.rightText: And all vision is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee; and he saith, I cannot, for it is sealed:

units.leftText: and the book is delivered to one who is not educated, saying, “Read this, please;” and he says, “I can’t read.”
units.rightText: and the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee; and he saith, I am not learned.

units.leftText: The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which has been taught;
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw nigh unto me, and with their mouth and with their lips do honor me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which hath been taught them;

units.leftText: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous work among this people, even a marvelous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men will perish, and the understanding of their prudent men will be hidden.”
units.rightText: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

units.leftText: Woe to those who deeply hide their counsel from the LORD, and whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us?” and “Who knows us?”
units.rightText: Woe unto them that hide deep their counsel from Jehovah, and whose works are in the dark, and that say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?

units.leftText: You turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought to be like clay, that the thing made should say about him who made it, “He didn’t make me;” or the thing formed say of him who formed it, “He has no understanding”?
units.rightText: Ye turn things upside down! Shall the potter be esteemed as clay; that the thing made should say of him that made it, He made me not; or the thing formed say of him that formed it, He hath no understanding?

units.leftText: Isn’t it yet a very little while, and Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will be regarded as a forest?
units.rightText: Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?

units.leftText: In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of obscurity and out of darkness.
units.rightText: And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity and out of darkness.

units.leftText: The humble also will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: The meek also shall increase their joy in Jehovah, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: For the ruthless is brought to nothing, and the scoffer ceases, and all those who are alert to do evil are cut off—
units.rightText: For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scoffer ceaseth, and all they that watch for iniquity are cut off;

units.leftText: who cause a person to be indicted by a word, and lay a snare for one who reproves in the gate, and who deprive the innocent of justice with false testimony.
units.rightText: that make a man an offender in his cause, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just with a thing of nought.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says concerning the house of Jacob: “Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, neither shall his face grow pale.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale.

units.leftText: But when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the middle of him, they will sanctify my name. Yes, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
units.rightText: But when he seeth his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name; yea, they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall stand in awe of the God of Israel.

units.leftText: They also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will receive instruction.”
units.rightText: They also that err in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmur shall receive instruction.

units.leftText: “Woe to the rebellious children”, says the LORD, “who take counsel, but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin;
units.rightText: Woe to the rebellious children, saith Jehovah, that take counsel, but not of me; and that make a league, but not of my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin,

units.leftText: who set out to go down into Egypt without asking for my advice, to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!
units.rightText: that set out to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!

units.leftText: Therefore the strength of Pharaoh will be your shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.
units.rightText: Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.

units.leftText: For their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors have come to Hanes.
units.rightText: For their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors are come to Hanes.

units.leftText: They shall all be ashamed because of a people that can’t profit them, that are not a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.”
units.rightText: They shall all be ashamed because of a people that cannot profit them, that are not a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.

units.leftText: The burden of the animals of the South.
units.rightText: The burden of the beasts of the South.

units.leftText: For Egypt helps in vain, and to no purpose; therefore I have called her Rahab who sits still.
units.rightText: For Egypt helpeth in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I called her Rahab that sitteth still.

units.leftText: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come forever and ever.
units.rightText: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.

units.leftText: For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children who will not hear the LORD’s law;
units.rightText: For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of Jehovah;

units.leftText: who tell the seers, “Don’t see!” and the prophets, “Don’t prophesy to us right things. Tell us pleasant things. Prophesy deceits.
units.rightText: that say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits,

units.leftText: Get out of the way. Turn away from the path. Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.”
units.rightText: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.

units.leftText: Therefore the Holy One of Israel says, “Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it,
units.rightText: Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely thereon;

units.leftText: therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.
units.rightText: therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly in an instant.

units.leftText: He will break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing, so that there won’t be found among the broken pieces a piece good enough to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.”
units.rightText: And he shall break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing; so that there shall not be found among the pieces thereof a sherd wherewith to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.

units.leftText: For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
units.rightText: For thus said the Lord Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength. And ye would not:

units.leftText: but you said, “No, for we will flee on horses;” therefore you will flee; and, “We will ride on the swift;” therefore those who pursue you will be swift.
units.rightText: but ye said, No, for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift.

units.leftText: One thousand will flee at the threat of one. At the threat of five, you will flee until you are left like a beacon on the top of a mountain, and like a banner on a hill.
units.rightText: One thousand shall flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five shall ye flee: till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on a hill.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and therefore he will be exalted, that he may have mercy on you, for the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all those who wait for him.
units.rightText: And therefore will Jehovah wait, that he may be gracious unto you; and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for Jehovah is a God of justice; blessed are all they that wait for him.

units.leftText: For the people will dwell in Zion at Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.
units.rightText: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem; thou shalt weep no more; he will surely be gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear, he will answer thee.

units.leftText: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers;
units.rightText: And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be hidden anymore, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers;

units.leftText: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
units.rightText: and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it; when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.

units.leftText: You shall defile the overlaying of your engraved images of silver, and the plating of your molten images of gold. You shall cast them away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, “Go away!”
units.rightText: And ye shall defile the overlaying of thy graven images of silver, and the plating of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as an unclean thing; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.

units.leftText: He will give the rain for your seed, with which you will sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground will be rich and plentiful. In that day, your livestock will feed in large pastures.
units.rightText: And he will give the rain for thy seed, wherewith thou shalt sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground, and it shall be fat and plenteous. In that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures;

units.leftText: The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory feed, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
units.rightText: the oxen likewise and the young asses that till the ground shall eat savory provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.

units.leftText: There will be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
units.rightText: And there shall be upon every lofty mountain, and upon every high hill, brooks and streams of waters, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

units.leftText: Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.
units.rightText: Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah bindeth up the hurt of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.

units.leftText: Behold, the LORD’s name comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation. His tongue is as a devouring fire.
units.rightText: Behold, the name of Jehovah cometh from far, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire;

units.leftText: His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction. A bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.
units.rightText: and his breath is as an overflowing stream, that reacheth even unto the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction: and a bridle that causeth to err shall be in the jaws of the peoples.

units.leftText: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept, and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to the LORD’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
units.rightText: Ye shall have a song as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come unto the mountain of Jehovah, to the Rock of Israel.

units.leftText: The LORD will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, and tempest, and hailstones.

units.leftText: For through the LORD’s voice the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.
units.rightText: For through the voice of Jehovah shall the Assyrian be dismayed; with his rod will he smite him.

units.leftText: Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which the LORD will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.
units.rightText: And every stroke of the appointed staff, which Jehovah shall lay upon him, shall be with the sound of tabrets and harps; and in battles with the brandishing of his arm will he fight with them.

units.leftText: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, it is prepared for the king. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. The LORD’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
units.rightText: For a Topheth is prepared of old; yea, for the king it is made ready; he hath made it deep and large; the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of Jehovah, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

units.leftText: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
units.rightText: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek Jehovah!

units.leftText: Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster,
units.rightText: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evil-doers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.

units.leftText: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God;
units.rightText: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit: and when Jehovah shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall stumble, and he that is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.

units.leftText: For the LORD says to me,
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah unto me, As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so will Jehovah of hosts come down to fight upon mount Zion, and upon the hill thereof.

units.leftText: As birds hovering, so the LORD of Armies will protect Jerusalem.
units.rightText: As birds hovering, so will Jehovah of hosts protect Jerusalem; he will protect and deliver it, he will pass over and preserve it.

units.leftText: Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
units.rightText: Turn ye unto him from whom ye have deeply revolted, O children of Israel.

units.leftText: For in that day everyone shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold—sin which your own hands have made for you.
units.rightText: For in that day they shall cast away every man his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin.

units.leftText: “The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man;
units.rightText: And the Assyrian shall fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of men, shall devour him; and he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall become subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: His rock will pass away by reason of terror,
units.rightText: And his rock shall pass away by reason of terror, and his princes shall be dismayed at the ensign, saith Jehovah, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness,
units.rightText: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.

units.leftText: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind,
units.rightText: And a man shall be as a hiding-place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a great rock in a weary land.

units.leftText: The eyes of those who see will not be dim,
units.rightText: And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.

units.leftText: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge,
units.rightText: And the heart of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.

units.leftText: The fool will no longer be called noble,
units.rightText: The fool shall be no more called noble, nor the churl said to be bountiful.

units.leftText: For the fool will speak folly,
units.rightText: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise profaneness, and to utter error against Jehovah, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.

units.leftText: The ways of the scoundrel are evil.
units.rightText: And the instruments of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the meek with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.

units.leftText: But the noble devises noble things,
units.rightText: But the noble deviseth noble things; and in noble things shall he continue.

units.leftText: Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice!
units.rightText: Rise up, ye women that are at ease, and hear my voice; ye careless daughters, give ear unto my speech.

units.leftText: For days beyond a year you will be troubled, you careless women;
units.rightText: For days beyond a year shall ye be troubled, ye careless women; for the vintage shall fail, the ingathering shall not come.

units.leftText: Tremble, you women who are at ease!
units.rightText: Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be troubled, ye careless ones; strip you, and make you bare, and gird sackcloth upon your loins.

units.leftText: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields,
units.rightText: They shall smite upon the breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.

units.leftText: Thorns and briers will come up on my people’s land;
units.rightText: Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city.

units.leftText: For the palace will be forsaken.
units.rightText: For the palace shall be forsaken; the populous city shall be deserted; the hill and the watch-tower shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;

units.leftText: until the Spirit is poured on us from on high,
units.rightText: until the Spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be esteemed as a forest.

units.leftText: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness;
units.rightText: Then justice shall dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness shall abide in the fruitful field.

units.leftText: The work of righteousness will be peace,
units.rightText: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence for ever.

units.leftText: My people will live in a peaceful habitation,
units.rightText: And my people shall abide in a peaceable habitation, and in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting-places.

units.leftText: though hail flattens the forest,
units.rightText: But it shall hail in the downfall of the forest; and the city shall be utterly laid low.

units.leftText: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters,
units.rightText: Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth the feet of the ox and the ass.

units.leftText: Woe to you who destroy, but you weren’t destroyed,
units.rightText: Woe to thee that destroyest, and thou wast not destroyed; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! When thou hast ceased to destroy, thou shalt be destroyed; and when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.

units.leftText: LORD, be gracious to us. We have waited for you.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou our arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.

units.leftText: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled.
units.rightText: At the noise of the tumult the peoples are fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations are scattered.

units.leftText: Your plunder will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers.
units.rightText: And your spoil shall be gathered as the caterpillar gathereth: as locusts leap shall men leap upon it.

units.leftText: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high.
units.rightText: Jehovah is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

units.leftText: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge.
units.rightText: And there shall be stability in thy times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge: the fear of Jehovah is thy treasure.

units.leftText: Behold, their valiant ones cry outside;
units.rightText: Behold, their valiant ones cry without; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.

units.leftText: The highways are desolate.
units.rightText: The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: the enemy hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth not man.

units.leftText: The land mourns and languishes.
units.rightText: The land mourneth and languisheth; Lebanon is confounded and withereth away; Sharon is like a desert; and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

units.leftText: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Now will I arise, saith Jehovah; now will I lift up myself; now will I be exalted.

units.leftText: You will conceive chaff.
units.rightText: Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath is a fire that shall devour you.

units.leftText: The peoples will be like the burning of lime,
units.rightText: And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut down, that are burned in the fire.

units.leftText: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done;
units.rightText: Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.

units.leftText: The sinners in Zion are afraid.
units.rightText: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling hath seized the godless ones: Who among us can dwell with the devouring fire? who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?

units.leftText: He who walks righteously
units.rightText: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from taking a bribe, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from looking upon evil:

units.leftText: he will dwell on high.
units.rightText: He shall dwell on high; his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks; his bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.

units.leftText: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty.
units.rightText: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold a land that reacheth afar.

units.leftText: Your heart will meditate on the terror.
units.rightText: Thy heart shall muse on the terror: Where is he that counted, where is he that weighed the tribute? where is he that counted the towers?

units.leftText: You will no longer see the fierce people,
units.rightText: Thou shalt not see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that thou canst not comprehend, of a strange tongue that thou canst not understand.

units.leftText: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals.
units.rightText: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tent that shall not be removed, the stakes whereof shall never be plucked up, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken.

units.leftText: But there the LORD will be with us in majesty,
units.rightText: But there Jehovah will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby.

units.leftText: For the LORD is our judge.
units.rightText: For Jehovah is our judge, Jehovah is our lawgiver, Jehovah is our king; he will save us.

units.leftText: Your rigging is untied.
units.rightText: Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not strengthen the foot of their mast, they could not spread the sail: then was the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame took the prey.

units.leftText: The inhabitant won’t say, “I am sick.”
units.rightText: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.

units.leftText: Come near, you nations, to hear!
units.rightText: Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye peoples: let the earth hear, and the fulness thereof; the world, and all things that come forth from it.

units.leftText: For the LORD is enraged against all the nations,
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath indignation against all the nations, and wrath against all their host: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.

units.leftText: Their slain will also be cast out,
units.rightText: Their slain also shall be cast out, and the stench of their dead bodies shall come up; and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.

units.leftText: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved.
units.rightText: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll; and all their host shall fade away, as the leaf fadeth from off the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig-tree.

units.leftText: For my sword has drunk its fill in the sky.
units.rightText: For my sword hath drunk its fill in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Edom, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.

units.leftText: The LORD’s sword is filled with blood.
units.rightText: The sword of Jehovah is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for Jehovah hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

units.leftText: The wild oxen will come down with them,
units.rightText: And the wild-oxen shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls: and their land shall be drunken with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.

units.leftText: For the LORD has a day of vengeance,
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

units.leftText: Its streams will be turned into pitch,
units.rightText: And the streams of Edom shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.

units.leftText: It won’t be quenched night or day.
units.rightText: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

units.leftText: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it.
units.rightText: But the pelican and the porcupine shall possess it; and the owl and the raven shall dwell therein: and he will stretch over it the line of confusion, and the plummet of emptiness.

units.leftText: They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there;
units.rightText: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.

units.leftText: Thorns will come up in its palaces,
units.rightText: And thorns shall come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in the fortresses thereof; and it shall be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.

units.leftText: The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves,
units.rightText: And the wild beasts of the desert shall meet with the wolves, and the wild goat shall cry to his fellow; yea, the night-monster shall settle there, and shall find her a place of rest.

units.leftText: The arrow snake will make her nest there,
units.rightText: There shall the dart-snake make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shade; yea, there shall the kites be gathered, every one with her mate.

units.leftText: Search in the book of the LORD, and read:
units.rightText: Seek ye out of the book of Jehovah, and read: no one of these shall be missing, none shall want her mate; for my mouth, it hath commanded, and his Spirit, it hath gathered them.

units.leftText: He has cast the lot for them,
units.rightText: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever; from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

units.leftText: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad.
units.rightText: The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.

units.leftText: It will blossom abundantly,
units.rightText: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing; the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon: they shall see the glory of Jehovah, the excellency of our God.

units.leftText: Strengthen the weak hands,
units.rightText: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.

units.leftText: Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong!
units.rightText: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God; he will come and save you.

units.leftText: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened,
units.rightText: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

units.leftText: Then the lame man will leap like a deer,
units.rightText: Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall sing; for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.

units.leftText: The burning sand will become a pool,
units.rightText: And the glowing sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water: in the habitation of jackals, where they lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes.

units.leftText: A highway will be there, a road,
units.rightText: And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for the redeemed: the wayfaring men, yea fools, shall not err therein.

units.leftText: No lion will be there,
units.rightText: No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up thereon; they shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there:

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s ransomed ones will return,
units.rightText: and the ransomed of Jehovah shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads: they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

units.leftText: Now in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all of the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.

units.leftText: The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with a large army. He stood by the aqueduct from the upper pool in the fuller’s field highway.
units.rightText: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.

units.leftText: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph the recorder came out to him.
units.rightText: Then came forth unto him Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.

units.leftText: Rabshakeh said to them, “Now tell Hezekiah, ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What confidence is this in which you trust?
units.rightText: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

units.leftText: I say that your counsel and strength for the war are only vain words. Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
units.rightText: I say, thy counsel and strength for the war are but vain words: now on whom dost thou trust, that thou hast rebelled against me?

units.leftText: Behold, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt, which if a man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
units.rightText: Behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt, whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust on him.

units.leftText: But if you tell me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ isn’t that he whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You shall worship before this altar’?”
units.rightText: But if thou say unto me, We trust in Jehovah our God: is not that he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and hath said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?

units.leftText: Now therefore, please make a pledge to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them.
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray thee, give pledges to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.

units.leftText: How then can you turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put your trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
units.rightText: How then canst thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

units.leftText: Have I come up now without the LORD against this land to destroy it? The LORD said to me, “Go up against this land, and destroy it.”’”
units.rightText: And am I now come up without Jehovah against this land to destroy it? Jehovah said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

units.leftText: Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Don’t speak to us in the Jews’ language in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”
units.rightText: Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews’ language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall.

units.leftText: But Rabshakeh said, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”
units.rightText: But Rabshakeh said, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own water with you?

units.leftText: Then Rabshakeh stood, and called out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
units.rightText: Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said, Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: The king says, ‘Don’t let Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you.
units.rightText: Thus saith the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you:

units.leftText: Don’t let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, “The LORD will surely deliver us. This city won’t be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”’
units.rightText: neither let Hezekiah make you trust in Jehovah, saying, Jehovah will surely deliver us; this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: Don’t listen to Hezekiah, for the king of Assyria says, ‘Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and each of you eat from his vine, and each one from his fig tree, and each one of you drink the waters of his own cistern;
units.rightText: Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig-tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern;

units.leftText: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
units.rightText: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

units.leftText: Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, “The LORD will deliver us.” Have any of the gods of the nations delivered their lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?
units.rightText: Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, Jehovah will deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

units.leftText: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
units.rightText: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

units.leftText: Who are they among all the gods of these countries that have delivered their country out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”
units.rightText: Who are they among all the gods of these countries, that have delivered their country out of my hand, that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?

units.leftText: But they remained silent, and said nothing in reply, for the king’s commandment was, “Don’t answer him.”
units.rightText: But they held their peace, and answered him not a word; for the king’s commandment was, saying, Answer him not.

units.leftText: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
units.rightText: Then came Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, that was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

units.leftText: When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
units.rightText: And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, unto Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.

units.leftText: They said to him, “Hezekiah says, ‘Today is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to give birth.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of contumely; for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth.

units.leftText: It may be the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’”
units.rightText: It may be Jehovah thy God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which Jehovah thy God hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is left.

units.leftText: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
units.rightText: So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

units.leftText: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master, ‘The LORD says, “Don’t be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
units.rightText: And Isaiah said unto them, Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith Jehovah, Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

units.leftText: Behold, I will put a spirit in him and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”
units.rightText: Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear tidings, and shall return unto his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

units.leftText: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he heard that he had departed from Lachish.
units.rightText: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah; for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.

units.leftText: He heard news concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “He has come out to fight against you.” When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
units.rightText: And he heard say concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, He is come out to fight against thee. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

units.leftText: “Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, ‘Don’t let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Jerusalem won’t be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”
units.rightText: Thus shall ye speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God in whom thou trustest deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly. Shall you be delivered?
units.rightText: Behold, thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly: and shalt thou be delivered?

units.leftText: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?
units.rightText: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden that were in Telassar?

units.leftText: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?’”
units.rightText: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?

units.leftText: Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the LORD’s house, and spread it before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and Hezekiah went up unto the house of Jehovah, and spread it before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying,
units.rightText: And Hezekiah prayed unto Jehovah, saying,

units.leftText: “LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, who is enthroned among the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
units.rightText: O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, that sittest above the cherubim, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.

units.leftText: Turn your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and behold. Hear all of the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to defy the living God.
units.rightText: Incline thine ear, O Jehovah, and hear; open thine eyes, O Jehovah, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, who hath sent to defy the living God.

units.leftText: Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the countries and their land,
units.rightText: Of a truth, Jehovah, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries, and their land,

units.leftText: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.
units.rightText: and have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.

units.leftText: Now therefore, LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the LORD, even you only.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, O Jehovah our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Jehovah, even thou only.

units.leftText: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “The LORD, the God of Israel says, ‘Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
units.rightText: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent unto Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,

units.leftText: this is the word which the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
units.rightText: this is the word which Jehovah hath spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion hath despised thee and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.

units.leftText: Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Whom hast thou defied and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: By your servants, you have defied the Lord, and have said, “With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees. I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.
units.rightText: By thy servants hast thou defied the Lord, and hast said, With the multitude of my chariots am I come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon; and I will cut down the tall cedars thereof, and the choice fir-trees thereof; and I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field;

units.leftText: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt.”
units.rightText: I have digged and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet will I dry up all the rivers of Egypt.

units.leftText: “‘Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.
units.rightText: Hast thou not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? now have I brought it to pass, that it should be thine to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.

units.leftText: Therefore their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.
units.rightText: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power, they were dismayed and confounded; they were as the grass of the field, and as the green herb, as the grass on the housetops, and as a field of grain before it is grown up.

units.leftText: But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.
units.rightText: But I know thy sitting down, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy raging against me.

units.leftText: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.
units.rightText: Because of thy raging against me, and because thine arrogancy is come up into mine ears, therefore will I put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.

units.leftText: “‘This shall be the sign to you: You will eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from it; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee: ye shall eat this year that which groweth of itself, and in the second year that which springeth of the same; and in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit thereof.

units.leftText: The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
units.rightText: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

units.leftText: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.’
units.rightText: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and out of mount Zion they that shall escape. The zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this.

units.leftText: “Therefore the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come unto this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither shall he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.

units.leftText: He will return the way that he came, and he won’t come to this city,’ says the LORD.
units.rightText: By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and he shall not come unto this city, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: ‘For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.’”
units.rightText: For I will defend this city to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s angel went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand; and when men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.

units.leftText: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went away, returned to Nineveh, and stayed there.
units.rightText: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

units.leftText: As he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esar-haddon his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: In those days Hezekiah was sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.’”
units.rightText: In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Set thy house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.
leftNotes: 38:1 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
units.rightText: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, and prayed unto Jehovah,

units.leftText: and said, “Remember now, LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.
units.rightText: and said, Remember now, O Jehovah, I beseech thee, how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight. And Hezekiah wept sore.

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s word came to Isaiah, saying,
units.rightText: Then came the word of Jehovah to Isaiah, saying,

units.leftText: “Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘The LORD, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
units.rightText: Go, and say to Hezekiah, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years.

units.leftText: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
units.rightText: And I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city.

units.leftText: This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has spoken.
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee from Jehovah, that Jehovah will do this thing that he hath spoken:

units.leftText: Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps.”’” So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down.
units.rightText: behold, I will cause the shadow on the steps, which is gone down on the dial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the dial whereon it was gone down.

units.leftText: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness:
units.rightText: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickness.

units.leftText: I said, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol.
units.rightText: I said, In the noontide of my days I shall go into the gates of Sheol:
leftNotes: 38:10 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: I said, “I won’t see the LORD,
units.rightText: I said, I shall not see Jehovah, even Jehovah in the land of the living:
leftNotes: 38:11 Hebrew: יה Yah

units.leftText: My dwelling is removed,
units.rightText: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me as a shepherd’s tent:

units.leftText: I waited patiently until morning.
units.rightText: I quieted myself until morning; as a lion, so he breaketh all my bones:

units.leftText: I chattered like a swallow or a crane.
units.rightText: Like a swallow or a crane, so did I chatter;

units.leftText: What will I say?
units.rightText: What shall I say? he hath both spoken unto me, and himself hath done it:

units.leftText: Lord, men live by these things;
units.rightText: O Lord, by these things men live;

units.leftText: Behold, for peace I had great anguish,
units.rightText: Behold, it was for my peace that I had great bitterness:

units.leftText: For Sheol can’t praise you.
units.rightText: For Sheol cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee:
leftNotes: 38:18 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: The living, the living, he shall praise you, as I do today.
units.rightText: The living, the living, he shall praise thee, as I do this day:

units.leftText: The LORD will save me.
units.rightText: Jehovah is ready to save me:

units.leftText: Now Isaiah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover.”
units.rightText: Now Isaiah had said, Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a plaster upon the boil, and he shall recover.

units.leftText: Hezekiah also had said, “What is the sign that I will go up to the LORD’s house?”
units.rightText: Hezekiah also had said, What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of Jehovah?

units.leftText: At that time, Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, for he heard that he had been sick, and had recovered.
units.rightText: At that time Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

units.leftText: Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show them.
units.rightText: And Hezekiah was glad of them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah showed them not.

units.leftText: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah, and asked him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?”
units.rightText: Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.

units.leftText: Then he asked, “What have they seen in your house?”
units.rightText: Then said he, What have they seen in thy house? And Hezekiah answered, All that is in my house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not showed them.

units.leftText: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Armies:
units.rightText: Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Hear the word of Jehovah of hosts:

units.leftText: ‘Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up until today, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.
units.rightText: Behold, the days are coming, when all that is in thy house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: ‘They will take away your sons who will issue from you, whom you shall father, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace.’”
units.rightText: And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, whom thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

units.leftText: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The LORD’s word which you have spoken is good.” He said moreover, “For there will be peace and truth in my days.”
units.rightText: Then said Hezekiah unto Isaiah, Good is the word of Jehovah which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.

units.leftText: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
units.rightText: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.

units.leftText: “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.”
units.rightText: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem; and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she hath received of Jehovah’s hand double for all her sins.

units.leftText: The voice of one who calls out,
units.rightText: The voice of one that crieth, Prepare ye in the wilderness the way of Jehovah; make level in the desert a highway for our God.

units.leftText: Every valley shall be exalted,
units.rightText: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low; and the uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain:

units.leftText: The LORD’s glory shall be revealed,
units.rightText: and the glory of Jehovah shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken it.

units.leftText: The voice of one saying, “Cry out!”
units.rightText: The voice of one saying, Cry. And one said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field.

units.leftText: The grass withers,
units.rightText: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth, because the breath of Jehovah bloweth upon it; surely the people is grass.

units.leftText: The grass withers,
units.rightText: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth; but the word of our God shall stand forever.

units.leftText: You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain.
units.rightText: O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion, get thee up on a high mountain; O thou that tellest good tidings to Jerusalem, lift up thy voice with strength; lift it up, be not afraid; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold, your God!

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord GOD will come as a mighty one,
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord Jehovah will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him: Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

units.leftText: He will feed his flock like a shepherd.
units.rightText: He will feed his flock like a shepherd, he will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and will gently lead those that have their young.

units.leftText: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand,
units.rightText: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?

units.leftText: Who has directed the LORD’s Spirit,
units.rightText: Who hath directed the Spirit of Jehovah, or being his counsellor hath taught him?

units.leftText: Who did he take counsel with,
units.rightText: With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed to him the way of understanding?

units.leftText: Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket,
units.rightText: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are accounted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.

units.leftText: Lebanon is not sufficient to burn,
units.rightText: And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: All the nations are like nothing before him.
units.rightText: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are accounted by him as less than nothing, and vanity.

units.leftText: To whom then will you liken God?
units.rightText: To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?

units.leftText: A workman has cast an image,
units.rightText: The image, a workman hath cast it, and the goldsmith overlayeth it with gold, and casteth for it silver chains.

units.leftText: He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot.
units.rightText: He that is too impoverished for such an oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a skilful workman to set up a graven image, that shall not be moved.

units.leftText: Haven’t you known?
units.rightText: Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?

units.leftText: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth,
units.rightText: It is he that sitteth above the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in;

units.leftText: who brings princes to nothing,
units.rightText: that bringeth princes to nothing; that maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.

units.leftText: They are planted scarcely.
units.rightText: Yea, they have not been planted; yea, they have not been sown; yea, their stock hath not taken root in the earth: moreover he bloweth upon them, and they wither, and the whirlwind taketh them away as stubble.

units.leftText: “To whom then will you liken me?
units.rightText: To whom then will ye liken me, that I should be equal to him? saith the Holy One.

units.leftText: Lift up your eyes on high,
units.rightText: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who hath created these, that bringeth out their host by number; he calleth them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and for that he is strong in power, not one is lacking.

units.leftText: Why do you say, Jacob,
units.rightText: Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way is hid from Jehovah, and the justice due to me is passed away from my God?

units.leftText: Haven’t you known?
units.rightText: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard? The everlasting God, Jehovah, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary; there is no searching of his understanding.

units.leftText: He gives power to the weak.
units.rightText: He giveth power to the faint; and to him that hath no might he increaseth strength.

units.leftText: Even the youths faint and get weary,
units.rightText: Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall:

units.leftText: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength.
units.rightText: but they that wait for Jehovah shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not faint.

units.leftText: “Keep silent before me, islands,
units.rightText: Keep silence before me, O islands; and let the peoples renew their strength: let them come near; then let them speak; let us come near together to judgment.

units.leftText: Who has raised up one from the east?
units.rightText: Who hath raised up one from the east, whom he calleth in righteousness to his foot? he giveth nations before him, and maketh him rule over kings; he giveth them as the dust to his sword, as the driven stubble to his bow.

units.leftText: He pursues them
units.rightText: He pursueth them, and passeth on safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.

units.leftText: Who has worked and done it,
units.rightText: Who hath wrought and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last, I am he.

units.leftText: The islands have seen, and fear.
units.rightText: The isles have seen, and fear; the ends of the earth tremble; they draw near, and come.

units.leftText: Everyone helps his neighbor.
units.rightText: They help every one his neighbor; and every one saith to his brother, Be of good courage.

units.leftText: So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith.
units.rightText: So the carpenter encourageth the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smiteth the anvil, saying of the soldering, It is good; and he fasteneth it with nails, that it should not be moved.

units.leftText: “But you, Israel, my servant,
units.rightText: But thou, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,

units.leftText: you whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth,
units.rightText: thou whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from the corners thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant, I have chosen thee and not cast thee away;

units.leftText: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you.
units.rightText: fear thou not, for I am with thee; be not dismayed, for I am thy God; I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

units.leftText: Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded.
units.rightText: Behold, all they that are incensed against thee shall be put to shame and confounded: they that strive with thee shall be as nothing, and shall perish.

units.leftText: You will seek them, and won’t find them,
units.rightText: Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them, even them that contend with thee: they that war against thee shall be as nothing, and as a thing of nought.

units.leftText: For I, the LORD your God, will hold your right hand,
units.rightText: For I, Jehovah thy God, will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid, you worm Jacob,
units.rightText: Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith Jehovah, and thy Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth.
units.rightText: Behold, I have made thee to be a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth; thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff.

units.leftText: You will winnow them,
units.rightText: Thou shalt winnow them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them; and thou shalt rejoice in Jehovah, thou shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none.
units.rightText: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst; I, Jehovah, will answer them, I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

units.leftText: I will open rivers on the bare heights,
units.rightText: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.

units.leftText: I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness.
units.rightText: I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, and the oil-tree; I will set in the desert the fir-tree, the pine, and the box-tree together:

units.leftText: that they may see, know, consider, and understand together,
units.rightText: that they may see, and know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of Jehovah hath done this, and the Holy One of Israel hath created it.

units.leftText: Produce your cause,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Produce your cause, saith Jehovah; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob.

units.leftText: “Let them announce and declare to us what will happen!
units.rightText: Let them bring forth, and declare unto us what shall happen: declare ye the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.

units.leftText: Declare the things that are to come hereafter,
units.rightText: Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods: yea, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and behold it together.

units.leftText: Behold, you are nothing,
units.rightText: Behold, ye are of nothing, and your work is of nought; an abomination is he that chooseth you.

units.leftText: “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come,
units.rightText: I have raised up one from the north, and he is come; from the rising of the sun one that calleth upon my name: and he shall come upon rulers as upon mortar, and as the potter treadeth clay.

units.leftText: Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know?
units.rightText: Who hath declared it from the beginning, that we may know? and beforetime, that we may say, He is right? yea, there is none that declareth, yea, there is none that showeth, yea, there is none that heareth your words.

units.leftText: I am the first to say to Zion, ‘Behold, look at them;’
units.rightText: I am the first that saith unto Zion, Behold, behold them; and I will give to Jerusalem one that bringeth good tidings.

units.leftText: When I look, there is no man,
units.rightText: And when I look, there is no man: even among them there is no counsellor, that, when I ask of them, can answer a word.

units.leftText: Behold, all of their deeds are vanity and nothing.
units.rightText: Behold, all of them, their works are vanity and nought; their molten images are wind and confusion.

units.leftText: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold,
units.rightText: Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delighteth: I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: He will not shout,
units.rightText: He will not cry, nor lift up his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.

units.leftText: He won’t break a bruised reed.
units.rightText: A bruised reed will he not break, and a dimly burning wick will he not quench: he will bring forth justice in truth.

units.leftText: He will not fail nor be discouraged,
units.rightText: He will not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set justice in the earth; and the isles shall wait for his law.

units.leftText: God the LORD,
units.rightText: Thus saith God Jehovah, he that created the heavens, and stretched them forth; he that spread abroad the earth and that which cometh out of it; he that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein:

units.leftText: “I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness.
units.rightText: I, Jehovah, have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thy hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles;

units.leftText: to open the blind eyes,
units.rightText: to open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison-house.

units.leftText: “I am the LORD.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah, that is my name; and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise unto graven images.

units.leftText: Behold, the former things have happened
units.rightText: Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare; before they spring forth I tell you of them.

units.leftText: Sing to the LORD a new song,
units.rightText: Sing unto Jehovah a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth; ye that go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the isles, and the inhabitants thereof.

units.leftText: Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices,
units.rightText: Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice, the villages that Kedar doth inhabit; let the inhabitants of Sela sing, let them shout from the top of the mountains.

units.leftText: Let them give glory to the LORD,
units.rightText: Let them give glory unto Jehovah, and declare his praise in the islands.

units.leftText: The LORD will go out like a mighty man.
units.rightText: Jehovah will go forth as a mighty man; he will stir up his zeal like a man of war: he will cry, yea, he will shout aloud; he will do mightily against his enemies.

units.leftText: “I have been silent a long time.
units.rightText: I have long time holden my peace; I have been still, and refrained myself: now will I cry out like a travailing woman; I will gasp and pant together.

units.leftText: I will destroy mountains and hills,
units.rightText: I will lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs; and I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.

units.leftText: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know.
units.rightText: And I will bring the blind by a way that they know not; in paths that they know not will I lead them; I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. These things will I do, and I will not forsake them.

units.leftText: “Those who trust in engraved images,
units.rightText: They shall be turned back, they shall be utterly put to shame, that trust in graven images, that say unto molten images, Ye are our gods.

units.leftText: “Hear, you deaf,
units.rightText: Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see.

units.leftText: Who is blind, but my servant?
